templates.why_chosen: The switch is the hub with two deliberately asymmetric spokes, an NF-compute server handling headers and an RDMA-memory server handling payloads, each returning results the switch's rebuilder reassembles in order.
templates.what_to_learn: A hub's spokes need not be identical: when two offload targets do genuinely different jobs, still draw them as parallel boxes at the same level, and colour-code the shared unit that threads through both, four packet flows here, so the reader can follow one flow out to its spoke and back.

templates.why_chosen: High-confidence rank-19 pick: the boxed programmable switch is the chip, with the multi-core NF server and RDMA server drawn outside it, and four color-coded packets trace the header and payload split across ten components.
templates.what_to_learn: Draw the switch's boundary as the chip and place the two external servers physically outside it, then give each flow its own packet colour rather than one arrow style so a reader can trace a single packet through splitter, storage and rebuilder; reserve dashed for outbound and solid for the return path.
